investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent 'BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 (+https://github.com/chriswatson6675/band_on_the_map)', no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official /agenda/ page, its homepage, two individual event detail pages, and (as a further passive check of a link the site's own head markup advertises) the site's public WordPress REST API single-post endpoint. The listing page carries no Event JSON-LD; each detail page embeds a genuinely structured, machine-readable 'google-event' data-attribute block (date+time, both start and end) that powers the page's own 'Add to Google Calendar' feature.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the official agenda page (https://badaboum.paris/agenda/) found a WordPress site with a custom 'evenement' post type, no calendar plugin, and no schema.org Event JSON-LD (its single JSON-LD block is Yoast SEO boilerplate: WebPage/BreadcrumbList/WebSite/Organization only). The page's own repeated static card markup states 39 real events with title, category tag, own detail-page URL, and a full French-language date (day+month+4-digit year) directly. Fetching two of those detail pages directly then each stated a genuinely structured, machine-readable calendar-data block (<div class="google-event" data-date-start=... data-h-start=... data-date-end=... data-h-end=...>) giving an exact start+end date AND time-of-day — a strictly better data path than the list page's own date-only text. As a further passive check, the page's own <link rel='https://api.w.org/post'> head markup advertises a public WordPress REST API endpoint (wp-json/wp/v2/evenement/{id}); fetching it (still a plain, unauthenticated GET) showed it carries only WordPress's own post-management date/modified timestamps and a free-text 'content.rendered' blob — genuinely useful as corroborating text, but NOT a structured event date/time field, so it was inspected and explicitly rejected as this source's own primary data path (see data_paths). This fully answers the investigation question at Level 1; no structural/browser escalation was needed.

venue_reference: Badaboum (concert/club venue, 2 rue des Taillandiers, 75011 Paris)

identity.notes: The retained agenda page's own JSON-LD 'Organization' block states name 'Badaboum' at the venue's own domain badaboum.paris. The retained homepage's own text directly states '2 Rue des Taillandiers 75011 Paris' — matching this task's assigned arrondissement/postcode. See venue_location below for an honest note on the exact house-number text ('2' vs. this task's '2 bis').

site_classification.platform: WordPress with a custom 'evenement' post type (confirmed via the page's own linked wp-json/wp/v2/evenement/{id} REST route). No calendar plugin, no schema.org Event JSON-LD (only Yoast SEO boilerplate). The list page states title+category+date-only text; each event's own detail page additionally embeds a genuinely structured, machine-readable <div class="google-event" data-date-start data-date-end data-h-start data-h-end> block (used by the page's own front-end JS to power an 'Add to Google Calendar' link) — a real, complete, first-party start+end instant, not merely prose text. The site's own public REST API (wp-json/wp/v2/evenement/{id}) was inspected and found NOT to expose this structured date/time at all (only post-management date/modified timestamps and free-text content), so it is not used as this source's data path.

venue_location.notes: Single-venue source. The venue's own retained homepage AND both sampled event detail pages' own rendered content consistently state '2 Rue des Taillandiers — 75011 Paris' (NO 'bis'). This investigation records the address EXACTLY as the source itself states it, honestly noting a discrepancy with this task's own assigned address ('2 bis rue des Taillandiers') — the source's own first-party text is treated as the governing fact here, per policy ('existing canonical/public data must not be mutated... merely to make parsing easier' cuts the other way too: an investigation must not silently reconcile a discrepancy by preferring an external brief over the source's own retained statement).

source_record_id.notes: No numeric id is exposed on the card itself (the WordPress post id, e.g. 1712, is only visible via the site's own linked REST API — see data_paths — not on the public-facing pages). Each card's own href is this source's own permanent '/evenement/{slug}/' WordPress permalink page, so the slug is used as source_record_id — the same documented judgement already accepted for badehaus-berlin/tempodrom-berlin/cafe-de-la-danse-paris/backstage-btm-paris.

event_url.notes: Each card's own href, stated directly.

price.notes: No price value is ever printed on a card or its own detail page — only a booking link out to a third-party platform (Shotgun, confirmed on both sampled pages). No first-party price text exists to record (the WP REST API's own rendered content text separately states 'FREE ENTRANCE FROM 4:30AM' for this specific sampled event, a genuinely interesting first-party fact, but it is a conditional/partial free-entry window rather than a general price statement, and was not observed consistently formatted across other sampled events, so it is not promoted to a generalised PROVEN price field here).
